newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK shares hit record on blue-chip profits,Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK shares hit record on blue-chip profits,Dow.

text.p: London's FTSE 100 share index charged into record territory on Thursday, spurred by positive reaction to a batch of blue-chip results and the Wall Street's bullish response to comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.

"All the ingredients were there for a good performance -- we've seen worries about Wall Street recede and earnings figures were good today," a dealer said. "Various bid rumours are still doing the rounds and even at these levels nobody wants to sell."
The FTSE 100 powered up 35.1 points or 0.81 percent to 4,395.2 by 1335 GMT with the FTSE 250 index of medium-sized companies also hitting a new high, up 23.4 at 4,702.0.
"We've really gone roaring up," another dealer said. "Wall Street was good, the results have been good, it's shaping up to be a cracking day."
The foundations of the rally were laid by Greenspan, who reversed some of the damage wreaked on Wall Street last week by his warnings on equity prices.

Instead of repeating last week's comment that Wall Street's ascent "raised questions of sustainability", Greenspan appeared to soften his tone in the second half of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on Wednesday.

He said the U.S. stock market was "properly priced" if Wall Street's assumptions about corporate profit growth proved correct. The Dow stormed ahead on his comments, ending 93 points higher at 6,946 after having been 46 points up as London closed on Wednesday.
Of six FTSE companies to announce annual results on Thursday, the market reacted positively to four.

Rolls-Royce Plc powered ahead after revealing its full-year figures. Profit figures also boosted betting and hotels firm Ladbroke Group Plc, industrial conglomerate BTR Plc and engineering group GKN Plc.
Pharmaceutical giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc headed lower after its results announcement, however, and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc also lost ground after initially gaining on its results.
The FTSE has risen 277 points or nearly seven percent since the start of the year. It closed at 4,118.5 on December 31.
Analysts say the market has been boosted by Wall Street's bull run as well as a relatively benign domestic interest rate environment and large inflows of cash from institutional investors.
Although the Bank of England wants to raise rates, the market remains convinced that the government will keep rates on hold before the British general election, which must be held by May 22.
Demand for shares has been so high that the market has regularly suffered stock shortages this year, squeezing prices even higher.
